knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: CK-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly distinguishes method of moments from maximum likelihood estimation?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The methods use different estimating principles and need not agree.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: MoM matches moments; MLE maximises the observed-data likelihood.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Assuming the methods are identical because they coincide in some models.

choices.label: Method of moments equates sample and model moments, while maximum likelihood maximises the likelihood of observed data.
Both methods always produce the same estimator.
Method of moments maximises the probability of the observed sample.
Maximum likelihood uses only the first population moment.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: CK-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which identity correctly expresses the mean squared error of an estimator T for parameter theta?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: MSE combines variance and squared bias; unbiasedness alone does not ensure minimum MSE.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: MSE equals variance plus squared bias.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating unbiasedness as sufficient for efficiency.
